[ASSISTANT_SAID] A lack of diversity in the workplace can result from a narrow focus on academic qualifications, as systemic barriers may prevent diverse backgrounds from obtaining these qualifications.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Overreliance on academic qualifications can stifle innovation and progress by creating homogeneity in the workplace.  
[USER] The user asked what can be done to address the issue of representation and inclusion for disadvantaged backgrounds in Western workplaces.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Employers should broaden their definition of talent beyond academic achievement to include a wider range of skills, qualities, and experiences.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Governments and employers should work together to improve access to education for disadvantaged backgrounds through financial support, mentorship, and guidance programs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Employers should implement diversity and inclusion policies to actively recruit, retain, and promote people from diverse backgrounds.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Employers should offer alternative pathways to employment, such as apprenticeships, traineeships, and internships, to help disadvantaged individuals gain work experience.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Employers should address unconscious biases and stereotypes that may hinder the recruitment and promotion of people from disadvantaged backgrounds.  
[USER] The user expressed frustration about the importance placed on academic qualifications over other skills and suggested that employers should give equal weight to both.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Employers should value both academic qualifications and practical skills, as both demonstrate different abilities essential for workplace success.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Academic qualifications show a person's ability to learn, while practical skills demonstrate the ability to apply knowledge in real-world situations.
